newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West power talked higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West power talked higher in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. Mid-West spot electricity was talked slightly higher Monday in thin trade with many players reluctant to do deals for October 1 delivery on the last day of September, industry sources said.
"People are kind of hesitant to schedule for tomorrow with September nearly over," one marketer said.

On-peak next day power for a 16-hour block for Tuesday in Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) was talked in the $14.00-16.00 range from Monday delivery at $12.00-15.50, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak MAPP power was pegged steady $7.50-9.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, the sources said.
On-peak prices in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) region for Tuesday delivery were discussed at $17.50-19.50 from Monday delivery at $16.50-19.50 per MWh.
Off-peak MAIN power was said to be steady to higher in the $11.00-12.50 from $9.50-11.00 late last week, the sources said.
October MAIN was assessed over a wide range of $15.50-18.50 per MWh.
In the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak power prices for Tuesday delivery were talked up steady at $17.00-20.00 per MWh.
Off peak ECAR was said to be unchanged in the $11.50-14.00 per MWh range.
October ECAR was talked in the $16.50-17.50 range, the sources said.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), on-peak power for Monday delivery in the north area was assessed higher near $17.00 from $15.00-16.00 for Monday delivery.
Off-peak was pegged at $10.00-11.00 per MWh.
In the south of SPP, power was pegged higher at near $18.00 from a range of $17.75-18.25 for Monday delivery.
Off peak was assessed near $12.00, the sources said.
October SPP was assessed steady in the $17.80-18.20 range, while November was pegged near $18.20-18.50 per MWh.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
